subject.title: /new and /reset should support @agent targeting in multi-agent channels

question: What should `/new` and `/reset` do when more than one configured agent could handle the channel and the user supplies no explicit target?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but choosing text `@agent`, native `agent:` parameters, and the no-target fallback affects session-state safety, command authorization, and existing multi-agent channel habits.

options.title: Require Explicit Target In Multi-Agent Rooms
options.body: Add text and native-command agent targeting, and make ambiguous destructive commands prompt or no-op instead of resetting a guessed agent.

options.title: Route First, Target Optional
options.body: Keep current route/binding behavior as the default and add `@agent` or native `agent:` only as an override.

options.title: Document Channel Isolation Only
options.body: Leave runtime unchanged and document dedicated channels, bindings, or per-account command naming as the supported workaround.

recommendation.title: Require Explicit Target In Multi-Agent Rooms
recommendation.body: Add text and native-command agent targeting, and make ambiguous destructive commands prompt or no-op instead of resetting a guessed agent.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product/security contract on Discord/native-command and reset semantics, and steipete has the strongest relevant history on those policy surfaces.
